title: Hypothesis Workshop — personal sketch
body:
Why this exists:
- current eval loops are heavyweight; need a tiny, fast loop for engineering + PMs to test response economics and fallback strategies in under an hour.
- goal: reduce decision latency (not build a full product). Start personal/teammate tool that can be promoted.

One-liner:
- Tiny sandbox to assemble short experiments (<=30 prompts), switch model/quant/batching, run simulated or tiny live samples, and get quick cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.

Must-have features (MVP-1):
- experiment canvas: prompt list, small golden set, quick label entry; save/load experiments as JSON.
- model toggles: pick model alias + variant (fp16, 4-bit, q8-like).
- runtime knobs: batch cap, max_tokens, prefix-cache on/off.
- metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency (sim or real), token counts, simple quality (binary + short note).
- compare view: side-by-side responses + token/cost delta.
- snapshot export: experiment config + responses + metrics as shareable JSON.

User stories (sketch):
- ML eng: compare fp16 vs 4-bit on same prompt set to estimate median latency and token cost; produce recommendation.
- PM: run 10 prompts across three fallback strategies to choose rollout candidate.
- Dev: attach snapshot to PR/Jira so reviewers can reproduce reasoning.

Acceptance criteria (MVP-1):
- define experiment (<=20 prompts), pick 2 variants, produce snapshot in <30 minutes.
- dashboard shows p50/p90 latency, token counts, basic quality metric.
- snapshots export clear JSON fields for easy linking.

Quick experiment matrix example:
- axes: model (redwood-small, rw-base, llama3x), quant (fp16/8/4), batch (1/4/8), prefix-cache (on/off)
- datasets: instruction-following (10), code-complete (8), short-qa (12)
- outputs: latency sim, token count, manual binary quality + notes

Implementation notes (rough):
- start CLI-first: experiment.json -> runner.py -> results.json. UI can be added later as tiny React page.
- runner: supports (a) fast sim using telemetry-derived latency/cost distributions, (b) small live runs using dev API key for sampling.
- telemetry stub: simple p50/p90/p99 distributions per model/seq-length from existing traces.
- storage: local snapshots; optional push to gist or S3 for sharing.
- snapshot metadata: git branch, PR id, runner user, timestamp.

UX light decisions:
- no auth; assumed dev environment. run-sim vs run-live toggle.
- response diff highlights token-level length and cost deltas.

Risks / open questions:
- safe usage: how to allow run-live without exposing prod budgets? need infra gating or soft limits.
- quality metric: binary correctness is cheap but noisy; need guidance for manual labeling.
- fidelity of sim: telemetry must be representative or people will distrust sim outputs.

Note: messy/short form intentionally. This is a personal scratchpad for iterating fast.
note: contains shorthand, TODOs, and rough fragments typical of a user scratchpad
action_items: Build prototype CLI runner (python) that accepts experiment.json and emits results.json
Create small telemetry stub (p50/p90/p99 distributions) from recent traces
Mock tiny one-page UI and share with Mika and Devon for quick feedback
